source_row.rationale: Bell's palsy is an idiopathic peripheral facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) paralysis causing unilateral facial drooping, inability to close the eye, and loss of the nasolabial fold. However, because its initial presentation can overlap with stroke, careful neurological assessment is essential to rule out central causes (such as forehead sparing, which is more typical of central/stroke-related facial weakness) before confirming a Bell's palsy diagnosis.
